items.text: Sources say: "The same leakage boundary applies to exogenous screening (F8): CrossAMI must be computed on the training window only.". What would happen if someone did it differently, and in what situations, if any, is doing it differently acceptable?

items.anchor: known_future_drivers should be used only for variables whose contemporaneous future values are genuinely known at prediction time, such as calendar flags or planned promotions.
items.text: Sources say: "Use `known_future_drivers` only for variables whose contemporaneous future values are genuinely known at prediction time, such as calendar flags, planned promotions, or externally scheduled variables.". What would happen if someone did it differently, and in what situations, if any, is doing it differently acceptable?

items.anchor: evaluation should be targeted exclusively at horizons in the
items.text: Sources prescribe: "A practitioner should target model evaluation exclusively at horizons in $\mathcal{H}_\varepsilon$ - lags outside this set carry no detectable predictive signal above the noise floor.". Think of the last time you did this. What result did you get, what had you expected, what did that result make you do next -- and what result would have sent you down a different path?

items.anchor: Any lag where a derived-feature profile exceeds the raw profile by more than estimation noise should be treated as a data-leakage candidate, not a genuine gain.
items.text: Sources say: "any lag where the derived profile exceeds the raw profile by more than estimation noise is a data-leakage candidate, not a genuine gain.". What would happen if someone did it differently, and in what situations, if any, is doing it differently acceptable?

items.anchor: Surrogates should be used whenever sample size permits, specifically when n is at least 200 and n_surrogates is at least 99.
items.text: Sources say: "Use surrogates whenever sample size permits ($n \ge 200$, `n_surrogates >= 99`).". What would happen if someone did it differently, and in what situations, if any, is doing it differently acceptable?

items.anchor: Epsilon should be defined relative to the surrogate upper band rather than as a global absolute constant, because an absolute threshold risks including noise lags or excluding informative ones as signal strength varies across series.
items.text: Sources say: "An absolute threshold risks including noise lags or excluding genuinely informative ones as signal strength varies across series.". What would happen if someone did it differently, and in what situations, if any, is doing it differently acceptable?

items.anchor: Any new selector that goes further than xami_sparse, such as PMIME-style or PC-stable with driver autohistory, must be introduced under a new method label so that shipped cross_pami and xami_sparse semantics are not silently extended.
